title: Support explicit PDS-managed pull, push, and conflict resolution
description: Future PDS-managed adapter for the document-centered architecture; existing sync is the starting implementation, not a new capability claim. Reuse the shared two-edge classifier and one-file @springleaf witnesses without storing base documents, sidecars, or a separately synchronized source file. Bind published identity to exact AT URI, never filename/path; use record CID preconditions for updates and report stale comparisons. Provide current-local/current-remote diff, explicit choose-local/choose-remote resolution, semantic fingerprints, post-write verification, and bounded interrupted-write recovery. Filename/path tidy remains independent. Preserve unknown record content and distinguish application-inflated content from actual PDS/offloaded payloads. Document that record updates can leave the Leaflet editor stale and a later native republish can overwrite them; management-mode changes must be explicit. Acceptance: coherent adapter design/implementation, offline classification and conditional-write tests, no accidental duplicate records after rename/path edit, no implicit deletion or cleanup, and public CLI documentation of lifecycle differences. No live writes without separate operator authorization. Origin: opencode://ses_e4900b8d7ffeDT9QuFwmKRAB7t, user-requested PDS alternative during redesign round 1.

title: Redesign explicit PDS-managed publishing with caller-selected record keys
description: Future alternative to the primary Leaflet-managed lifecycle; existing publish run already puts directly to the PDS. Carry that capability into the document-centered redesign deliberately: consume the same logical JSON/Markdown document and strip @springleaf, choose/validate an initial rkey explicitly rather than deriving it from filename, persist actual AT URI as identity, preserve it on updates, and surface path/routing constraints. A document has one chosen management mode, never simultaneous independent Leaflet/PDS writers. Preview the identity and the native lifecycle differences (application/editor linkage, publish versioning, revalidation, newsletter/mention/share behavior); do not assume firehose ingestion reproduces every native side effect or silently substitute this path for failed native publication. Acceptance: design and implementation of the explicit PDS-managed first-publication path with offline transport tests, key collision/conditional-create behavior, envelope stripping, identity preservation, and precise lifecycle tradeoff documentation. No live writes without separate operator authorization. Origin: opencode://ses_e4900b8d7ffeDT9QuFwmKRAB7t, user-requested PDS alternative during redesign round 1.
notes: Round-1 source verification: Leaflet 600c7b5f resolveDocumentFilter.ts matches actual publication-scoped record path before rkey fallback, so rkey/path need not inherently be equal for publication routing. Ordinary publishToPublication strips requested rkey and publishLeaflet resets path to /rkey; trusted admin importGhost can preserve a chosen source slug through native publication. No ordinary-user slug setter found in bounded source search; deployed behavior unverified. Carry both rkey selection and distinct path capability/routing collision checks into the PDS alternative without promising native lifecycle parity. Independent design references: design/document-sync1.gpt61s.md and design/document-sync1.gpt6a.md. Session opencode://ses_e4900b8d7ffeDT9QuFwmKRAB7t.

title: Explore lossless MDX-style document encoding for rich and unknown Leaflet blocks
description: Future exploration, not commissioned implementation. Investigate an MDX-like declarative markup encoding for Leaflet documents that preserves rich blocks and unknown block types alongside ordinary Markdown. Treat JSON and markup as alternative encodings of one logical document, not synchronized source/output copies. Preserve document metadata and embedded @springleaf state through frontmatter or an equivalent declarative mechanism; never execute arbitrary embedded code to decode a document. Define round-trip fidelity tests and explicit loss reports. Plain Markdown down-conversion should require --force-downconvert when canonical content cannot be preserved. Acceptance: a source-backed proposal identifying supported representations, unknown-block escape syntax, metadata handling, and representative lossless round-trip fixtures; no migration or live-write requirement. Origin: opencode://ses_e4900b8d7ffeDT9QuFwmKRAB7t, user-requested future ticket during document-centered redesign.
